title: Character & Conduct
description: General User → Beginner. Familiar teachings, broader basics and short everyday applications about honesty, trust, family, kindness, fairness, privacy and responsible conduct. All questions are Beginner level; scores indicate knowledge of these teachings, not a judgment of faith or personal character.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Which quality does Islam encourage in our speech?
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught that truthfulness leads toward righteousness.

questions.question: What does fulfilling an amanah mean?

options.text: Treating borrowed property as a gift
Taking care of a trust and giving what is due
Hiding what belongs to someone else
Keeping only promises that bring praise

questions.explanation: An amanah is a trust or responsibility. The Quran commands returning trusts to their rightful owners.

questions.question: How should a lawful promise be treated?

options.text: As something to break for amusement

questions.explanation: The Quran emphasizes fulfilling commitments and being accountable for them.

questions.question: What does the Quran command toward parents?
questions.explanation: The Quran joins worship of Allah alone with good treatment of parents.

questions.question: How should neighbors be treated?
questions.explanation: The Quran includes both near and more distant neighbors among those deserving good treatment.

questions.question: What does the Prophet encourage toward a guest?
questions.explanation: The Prophet linked faith with honoring guests and responsible conduct toward others.

questions.question: Which quality belongs in our treatment of children?
questions.explanation: The Prophet showed affection to children and emphasized mercy.

questions.question: Which quality makes our dealings more beautiful?
questions.explanation: The Prophet praised gentleness in how we deal with others.

questions.question: Which greeting does Islam encourage spreading?
questions.explanation: The Prophet encouraged greeting people, including those we do not already know.

questions.question: Which response to others' faults is praised in the Quran?
questions.explanation: The Quran praises restraining anger and pardoning people.

questions.question: What does sabr commonly mean?

options.text: Responding to every delay with abuse

questions.explanation: Sabr includes remaining steadfast in difficulty; the Quran encourages seeking help through patience and prayer.

questions.question: Which attitude is the opposite of looking down on people?
questions.explanation: The Quran warns against arrogant and boastful behavior toward others.

questions.question: What does the Quran say about offensive nicknames?

options.text: They prove friendship in every case
They are acceptable whenever others laugh

questions.explanation: The Quran forbids ridicule and calling others by offensive names.

questions.question: What is backbiting in the Prophet's explanation?

options.text: Mentioning an absent person's faults in a way they dislike

questions.explanation: The hadith explains backbiting and distinguishes it from false accusations. Legitimate reporting of harm is a separate matter.

questions.question: What should you seek before entering someone else's home?

options.text: A chance to look through their belongings
A reason to surprise them without warning

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches seeking permission and greeting the household before entering.

questions.question: Which quality must be maintained even toward someone we dislike?
questions.explanation: The Quran warns that dislike must not lead us away from justice.

questions.question: What does maintaining ties of kinship involve?

options.text: Cutting contact over every small annoyance

questions.explanation: The Prophet encouraged maintaining family relationships.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach about food and drink?

options.text: Treat waste as a sign of success
Always take more than you need

questions.explanation: The Quran permits eating and drinking while warning against excess.

questions.question: In what should people cooperate?
questions.explanation: The Quran encourages cooperation in righteousness and forbids cooperation in wrongdoing.

questions.question: Which quality did the Prophet praise among the best people?
questions.explanation: The Prophet praised excellence in character and manners.

questions.question: Does truthfulness matter when admitting a mistake is embarrassing?

options.text: Only if someone has recorded the mistake
Only when no friend is involved

questions.explanation: The call to truthfulness applies beyond easy or comfortable situations.

questions.question: Does borrowing something make you its owner?

options.text: Yes, if you keep it long enough
Yes, if you like it more
Yes, if the owner forgets to ask

questions.explanation: A borrowed item remains someone else's property and should be handled as a trust.

questions.question: Why should commitments not be made carelessly?

options.text: Because people are accountable for their commitments
Because breaking them always improves trust

questions.explanation: The Quran treats fulfilling commitments as a responsibility.

questions.question: Does respect for parents apply when they become elderly?

options.text: No, only young parents deserve respect
Yes, their age calls for care and respectful speech

questions.explanation: The Quran specifically emphasizes kindness when parents reach old age.

questions.question: Is saying every thought aloud always the best choice?

options.text: No, speech should be good and responsible
Yes, every thought must be announced
Only the loudest words count as good

questions.explanation: The Prophet taught speaking what is good or remaining silent.

questions.question: Does a comment become harmless gossip simply because it is true?

options.text: Yes, truth always removes any problem
No, a true hurtful comment may still be backbiting
Yes, if it is posted online
Yes, if enough people repeat it

questions.explanation: The hadith explains that an actual fault can still be the subject of backbiting; inventing it is slander.

questions.question: Why should harmful news be checked before it is spread?

options.text: To avoid harming people through ignorance
To make every rumor look certain

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches verification so that people are not harmed through careless reliance on reports.

questions.question: How should an unsupported suspicion about someone be treated?

options.text: Add details to make it convincing
Do not present it as an established fact

questions.explanation: The Quran warns against sinful suspicion. A guess is not established evidence.

questions.question: Should friendship change what is true or fair in a dispute?

options.text: Yes, a friend must always be declared right
Yes, facts matter only for strangers
Yes, fairness is unnecessary within a group

questions.explanation: Justice should not depend on whether we like the people involved.

questions.question: What did the Prophet identify as arrogance?

options.text: Rejecting truth and looking down on people

questions.explanation: The hadith distinguishes arrogance from enjoying a neat appearance.

questions.question: What does the Quran identify as the basis of honor before Allah?
questions.explanation: People and tribes are not grounds for superiority; the verse points to taqwa.

questions.question: What does controlling anger involve?

options.text: Answering every insult with an insult

questions.explanation: The Quran praises those who restrain anger; feeling upset does not require acting unjustly.

questions.question: Which attitude best reflects forgiveness for a minor personal offense?

options.text: Seeking chances to humiliate the person
Wishing to make every disagreement worse

questions.explanation: Forgiveness is praised. It does not require ignoring danger or abandoning protection from harm.

questions.question: What guidance does Luqman's advice give about the voice?

options.text: Shout to prove you are right
Never speak audibly in any situation
Use volume instead of good reasoning

questions.explanation: The advice encourages moderation and lowering the voice.

questions.question: What should a visitor do if asked to return another time?
questions.explanation: The Quran instructs visitors to turn back when asked to do so.

questions.question: What conduct brings blessing to a sale according to hadith?
questions.explanation: The Prophet praised honesty and openness between buyer and seller.

questions.question: How can you help a friend who is wronging someone?

options.text: Defend every action regardless of facts
Help hide the harm so it continues

questions.explanation: The Prophet explained that helping an oppressor means preventing their oppression.

questions.question: Which attitude does the hadith about helping others encourage?
questions.explanation: The hadith encourages practical support and relief of hardship.

questions.question: Does good conduct include avoiding harmful words as well as harmful actions?

options.text: Yes, both speech and actions matter

questions.explanation: The Prophet emphasized protecting others from harm through the tongue and hand.

questions.question: Is kindness limited only to one's closest family?

options.text: Only wealthy acquaintances should be added
No, neighbors, people in need and others also have rights

questions.explanation: The Quran names several groups deserving good treatment beyond one's parents and relatives.

questions.question: You accidentally damaged something at work. Which response follows truthfulness?

options.text: Explain honestly and help put it right
Invent an excuse to avoid all responsibility
Deny it despite knowing what happened

questions.explanation: Admitting a mistake and helping correct it puts truthfulness into practice.

questions.question: A friend lends you a book. What should you do with it?

options.text: Care for it and return it as agreed
Give it away as your own
Hide it when your friend asks

questions.explanation: Returning borrowed property respects the trust and its owner's rights.

questions.question: You agreed to help with a lawful task at a set time. What should you aim to do?

options.text: Ignore it because it was spoken, not written
Skip it just to see if anyone notices
Deny agreeing because something more fun appeared

questions.explanation: Treating a commitment seriously reflects the Quran's teaching about promises.

questions.question: An elderly parent asks you to repeat something. Which reply reflects good manners?

options.text: Shout that they should listen better
Insult them in front of others

questions.explanation: Respectful speech is particularly important when caring for aging parents.

questions.question: You learn that your unnecessary late-night noise disturbs a neighbor. What should you do?

options.text: Reduce the disturbance and be considerate
Increase the noise to annoy them
Tell others to disturb them too

questions.explanation: Being considerate about avoidable disturbance applies kindness toward neighbors.

questions.question: A guest arrives and you have only simple refreshments. Which response reflects hospitality?

options.text: Humiliate them because the food is simple
Welcome them warmly with what you can reasonably offer
Pretend expensive food is the only form of kindness
Treat them as unworthy of a greeting

questions.explanation: Hospitality includes a respectful welcome; kindness need not depend on luxury.

questions.question: A group uses a nickname that upsets a classmate. What should you do?

options.text: Keep using it because others laugh
Use the classmate's preferred respectful name

questions.explanation: Avoiding offensive names protects dignity and follows the Quran's instruction.

questions.question: Friends are sharing an absent person's faults just for entertainment. What is the best response?

options.text: Record the discussion to spread it
Say it is always acceptable if true
Avoid joining in and redirect the conversation

questions.explanation: The Quran and hadith warn against backbiting. Reporting harm to obtain help is a different matter.

questions.question: You receive an unverified accusation in a message. What should you do before repeating it?

options.text: Check its reliability instead of forwarding it as fact
Forward it quickly to every group

questions.explanation: Verification helps prevent unfair harm from rumors and misleading reports.

questions.question: Someone leaves their private phone messages open beside you. What should you do?

options.text: Respect their privacy and avoid snooping

questions.explanation: Avoiding spying is part of respecting another person's privacy.

questions.question: Someone you dislike is wrongly blamed. Which response reflects justice?

options.text: Support the false blame because you dislike them
Ignore known facts to win an argument

questions.explanation: Justice applies even when being fair benefits someone we do not like.

questions.question: You are angry during a disagreement. Which choice reflects self-control?

options.text: Bring their family into the argument
Pause and respond without insults or harm

questions.explanation: Restraining harmful reactions is a practical expression of controlling anger.

questions.question: A friend apologizes for a minor unintentional offense. Which response best reflects pardon?

options.text: Accept the apology without seeking revenge
Keep planning ways to embarrass them
Demand that everyone stop speaking to them
Repeat the incident to humiliate them

questions.explanation: Pardoning a minor personal offense puts the Quran's praise of forgiveness into practice.

questions.question: A new learner struggles with a basic task. Which response shows gentleness?

options.text: Explain patiently and encourage another try
Laugh at them in front of everyone
Make the task harder to punish them

questions.explanation: Gentleness helps us correct mistakes without needless humiliation.

questions.question: Someone younger points out a real mistake you made. What shows humility?

options.text: Reject it only because of their age
Mock them to protect your pride

questions.explanation: Accepting truth instead of dismissing the person is the opposite of arrogance.

questions.question: You have not checked on a relative for a while and can safely contact them. Which action maintains family ties?

options.text: Ignore them because they are not wealthy
Ask how they are and show sincere care

questions.explanation: Thoughtful contact is one everyday way to maintain good family relationships.

questions.question: At a meal, you can choose how much food to take. Which choice avoids waste?

options.text: Take a suitable portion and get more if needed
Pile up food only to throw it away
Treat leftovers as a reason to waste more

questions.explanation: Taking a reasonable amount applies the instruction to avoid wastefulness.

questions.question: You visit a home and are asked to come back later. What should you do?

options.text: Enter anyway because you know the family
Keep knocking to force a welcome

questions.explanation: Seeking permission includes accepting when entry is not convenient.

questions.question: You are selling a used phone with a known fault. What should you do?

options.text: Hide it until payment is complete
Claim the phone has no faults
Clearly tell the buyer about the fault
Use misleading photos to conceal it

questions.explanation: Honest disclosure respects the buyer and follows Prophetic guidance on trade.

questions.question: A friend asks you to help bully someone. What is the right response?

options.text: Refuse and help stop the harm safely

questions.explanation: Good friendship supports what is right; it does not help a person harm others.
